cases.question: On 29 July 2026, Sydney time, at which five-minute interval was NSW dispatch total demand highest across the whole day, and what was the level?

gold_numbers.label: NSW1 maximum dispatch total demand over 29 Jul AEST (interval ending 19:05 AEST)

expected.check: A correct answer gives the maximum over all 288 intervals of 29 July AEST (window (14:00Z 28 Jul, 14:00Z 29 Jul]) with its interval (ending 09:05Z = 19:05 AEST) and level; it must not report operational demand or a maximum over another window.

provenance.gold_method: Window = local day 29 Jul AEST = (2026-07-28T14:00Z, 2026-07-29T14:00Z], 288 intervals confirmed. Max of totaldemand_mw; tie check by equality with the max (one row); next-highest = second row by value.
queries: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00'

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, totaldemand_mw FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' ORDER BY totaldemand_mw DESC, interval_end_utc LIMIT 3

SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, totaldemand_mw FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' AND totaldemand_mw = (SELECT max(totaldemand_mw) FROM regionsum_5min WHERE region='NSW1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00')

cases.question: Which half-hour on 29 July 2026 (Brisbane time) had Queensland's highest operational demand, and how many MW was it?

gold_numbers.label: QLD1 maximum operational demand over 29 Jul AEST (half-hour 18:00-18:30 AEST), latest revision

expected.check: A correct answer gives the half-hour ending 08:30Z (18:00-18:30 AEST) and its operational demand from the latest revision; it must not give the runner-up half-hour ending 09:00Z (1 MW lower) or a dispatch total demand figure.

provenance.gold_method: Window = 48 half-hours of 29 Jul AEST, (2026-07-28T14:00Z, 2026-07-29T14:00Z]. Latest revision per half-hour = greatest available_at_utc ('updated' daily row). Max, tie check by equality, next-highest = second row.
queries: SELECT count(DISTINCT interval_end_utc) AS n FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00'

WITH latest AS (SELECT * FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1) SELECT row_id, interval_end_utc, revision, operational_demand_mw FROM latest ORDER BY operational_demand_mw DESC, interval_end_utc LIMIT 3

WITH latest AS (SELECT * FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='QLD1' AND interval_end_utc > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-28 14:00:00+00' AND interval_end_utc <= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-07-29 14:00:00+00' QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1) SELECT row_id FROM latest WHERE operational_demand_mw = (SELECT max(operational_demand_mw) FROM latest)

cases.question: For SA1, over the full local day of 29 July 2026 (midnight to midnight, Adelaide time), which 5-minute interval carried the day's top dispatch total demand, and what level did it hit?
cases.writer_notes: SA1 chosen: with F01 = QLD1 and NSW1/TAS1 excluded, the only other candidate is VIC1, whose 29 July 2026 day is development material. The SA1 day itself is not development material, but it contains one development half-hour (SA1, ending 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z); this cannot be avoided because every remaining region's day is development material. Fully held: 288 of 288 intervals. Tests the +09:30 offset.

cases.question: Thinking about the Victorian high-price event of 20 August 2026, how high did VIC1 dispatch total demand (TOTALDEMAND) go over that event's full window, and when was the top reached?
cases.writer_notes: Event VIC1-20260820T0910-hi: the only VIC1 event on 20 August 2026 and the only high-price event that day, so region + kind + date identify it uniquely. Not development material (unlike VIC1-20260728T2120-lo, SA1-20260731T0235-hi and the TAS1 6 August day; NSW1-20260731T0730-hi and SA1-20260729T1755-hi contain development half-hours). Fully held for total demand: 294 of 294 intervals. Identified by date rather than peak time so the question carries no time that might coincide with the answer.

cases.question: Based only on data published by noon Brisbane time on Sunday 5 October 2025, what was the highest operational demand in Queensland over that entire local day, and at what time?
cases.writer_notes: QLD1 local day 5 October 2025 (fully held, 48 half-hours; not development material; 24 hours since QLD1 has no daylight saving). Cutoff 2025-10-05T02:00:00Z = noon AEST, strictly inside the window. By the cutoff 8 half-hours have a public row (published 2025-10-04T21:26Z) and 40 do not (earliest publication 2025-10-05T21:26Z), so the whole-day maximum cannot be established as of the cutoff. The question asks for the whole day's maximum and names the cutoff in words that match the field.

cases.question: During Tasmania's 31 July 2026 high-price episode, how far did demand climb and when did it top out?
cases.writer_notes: Names no measure (only 'demand'), so a careful assistant must ask whether dispatch total demand or operational demand is meant. Otherwise in scope: TAS1, and the window of event TAS1-20260731T0730-hi (the only TAS1 event on 31 July 2026), which is fully held for both measures (288/288 and 48/48), so the missing measure is the only defect. Not development material.

cases.question: Taking South Australia's 7:30-8:00 am half-hour (Adelaide time, ACST) on 20 August 2026: what POE10, POE50 and POE90 operational demand values were in the final forecast run issued ahead of it, and what operational demand was actually measured?

gold_numbers.label: SA1 POE10, last run before 22:00Z, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug
SA1 POE50, last run before 22:00Z, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug
SA1 POE90, last run before 22:00Z, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug
SA1 actual operational demand, half-hour ending 22:30Z 19 Aug (latest revision)

expected.check: A correct answer converts 07:30-08:00 ACST (UTC+9:30) to the half-hour ending 2026-08-19T22:30Z, names the last run issued before 22:00Z and gives its POE10/50/90 and the actual; it must not treat the times as market time (UTC+10), which would select the half-hour ending 22:00Z.

provenance.gold_method: 07:30-08:00 ACST on 20 Aug -> 22:00Z-22:30Z on 19 Aug. Run = greatest issued_at_utc < target_start (22:00Z) among SA1 rows for target_end 22:30Z. Actual = latest-available revision.
queries: SELECT row_id, run_id, region, target_start_utc, target_end_utc, issued_at_utc, published_at_utc, available_at_utc, poe10_mw, poe50_mw, poe90_mw FROM opdemand_forecast WHERE region='SA1' AND target_end_utc = TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-19 22:30:00+00' AND issued_at_utc < target_start_utc ORDER BY issued_at_utc DESC LIMIT 1

SELECT row_id, region, interval_end_utc, revision, operational_demand_mw, published_at_utc, available_at_utc FROM opdemand_actual WHERE region='SA1' AND interval_end_utc IN (TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-19 22:30:00+00') QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY interval_end_utc ORDER BY available_at_utc DESC) = 1 ORDER BY interval_end_utc
